title: Soft probationary evictor and egress-cap trimmer for noisy-tenant storms
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Introduce a probationary eviction path for tenants that trigger noisy eviction loops; add an egress-cap trimmer to limit short-lived egress spikes that drive cross-region failovers. Default off, rollout via feature flag. Backwards-compatible.
description:
Motivation: We saw two incidents (2026-02-08, 2026-02-19) where tenant traffic patterns produced noisy eviction loops and large short-lived egress spikes that caused downstream region overfill and cascading failovers. Existing eviction is binary (healthy->evict) and can cause repeated oscillation for marginal tenants. This PR introduces a soft/probationary eviction state and a transient egress-cap trimmer to reduce sudden egress pressure while the probationary window evaluates a tenant's behavior.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a ProbationaryEvictor state machine: when a tenant crosses the eviction threshold we mark it PROBATION instead of immediately evicting. Probation enforces reduced concurrency and applies a slow-warmup to allow traffic to naturally subside.
- Implements EgressCapTrimmer: a local, low-latency limiter that observes short-window egress rate and trims per-tenant egress allowances by a configurable fraction (default 25%) for the probation window. This reduces instantaneous egress bursts that cause remote region egress quotas to saturate.
- Telemetry: new metrics (tenant.probation.entered, tenant.probation.exited, tenant.egress.trim_applied, probation.success_rate) and detailed spans for the probation transitions.
- Config & rollout: feature gate feature.probation_evictor (off by default). Two knobs: probation_window_ms (default 30000), egress_trim_fraction (default 0.25). Admin console controls added in runtime config.
- Safety: probation has an exponential backoff for repeated probation entries (cooldown), a hard evict fallback if a tenant continues to breach egress cap X times, and a dry-run mode that only emits telemetry.

Why this is safe to ship: the logic is opt-in by feature flag. Defaults are conservative and the hard-evict path remains available as a safety net. Telemetry allows us to measure candidate impact before aggressive rollout.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Jordan Wu (2026-02-26): "Can we avoid locking the egress trimmer on the hot path? Looks like we sample a 1s rolling window; prefer lock-free atomics to reduce contention."
  - Samir: "Updated trimmer to use lock-free ring buffer with atomics in b7c12d9; microbench numbers added to trimmer_test.go showing <1% overhead in median path."
- Mariana Lopez (2026-02-27): "What are the failure modes for probation? If the trimmer malfunctions could we throttle legitimate tenants? Need a clear kill-switch and canary plan."
  - Samir: "Added hard-evict fallback and a dry-run config. Also added runtime kill-switch config.probation.enabled and a canary rollout plan in the PR description. See integration test harness to validate safety."
- Evan Green (2026-02-28): "Telemetry looks good. Suggest adding an alert that fires if probation.success_rate drops under 60% after rollout."
  - Samir: "Added alert doc pointer in dashboards/PROBATION-234.json and a recommended alert rule in docs/reliability/probation_evictor.md."

CI summary:
- go test ./... -> pass
- lint -> pass (fixed a few style nits)
- perf-canary run -> pass on noisy-tenant scenario with expected reduction in egress tail; artifacts uploaded to infra-perf/probation/2026-03-01
- e2e in staging -> flaky initially due to race in test harness; fixed in e8ff4b0 and re-ran; pass

Rollout plan:
1) Enable feature.probation_evictor in staging for 48h in perf-canary with egress_trim_fraction=0.1
2) Monitor probation.success_rate and tenant.egress.trim_applied; ensure <5% of tenants see probation in steady state
3) Gradual rollout to 10% hosts in prod for 24h (kill-switch available)
4) Increase trim_fraction to 0.25 if metrics show continuing cross-region egress peaks

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals. Post-merge tasks: update operational runbook, schedule a DR drill with SRE to exercise kill-switch path.
